comments.text: People need to understand, this kind of corruption is par for the course in small towns and communities across this country. These small town sheriff offices and mayors offices and local governments, ( some not all), are currupt to the core. I live in Martin Co Kentucky, not very far from Letcher Co, and the curroptiin probably isn't to this level, but it's there for sure. What kind of corruption you might ask...... well here you go. Every drug head and dealer in the county will tell you, it's common knowledge, the current sheriff was the biggest dealer of prescription pain meds in the county before he became sheriff. He trains his deputies to be dirty and skirt the law, and violate people's rights. Several of them have been caught planting evidence on people. The sheriff himself has been under investigation for abuse of power and being over aggressive during arrests like three times in the last couple years. So much so that he couldn't even touch anyone, or put cuffs on anyone, or carry his sidearm. But whait..... there's more! We have a severe illegal Keno gambling problem all over the county and city seat. Business owners hiding illegal gambling facilities behind legit businesses all over the place and it's the worst kept secret in the state of Kentucky..... they don't even really try to hide it. The owners openly admit that the sheriff takes a cut of these illegal profits to look the other way.  In these small towns, everyone knows everyone. Some within the local government are life long friends, and even family, and they all operate like a giant currupt click. They hire from within and treat outsiders like trash, and they enforce laws and regulations uneventful based off of class and status. If your poor, or from the wrong family, or part of town, then you don't stand much of a chance. Listen there's good parts of living in a small, rural, low population town and community, but it's not all sunshine and rainbows.

The sherrif, who was deeply financially invested in the privately owned regional jail had bad blood with the DA because of the drug recovery early release program he had initiated.  That summer was the trial run of the program with a first wave of non-violent offenders serving time for drug-related convictions who were out on day/work/weekend release so long as they remained active participants in the program, passed drug screens & followed it's guidlines.  In time they could potentially be released early among other benefits.  Why this pissed the clearly corrupt sherrif off so bad that he and his goons harassed me under false reports is beyond me.
